key_insight: AdaLoRA-QAT enables clinically-faithful chest X‑ray segmentation with far fewer trainable parameters and INT8-ready models by combining adaptive low‑rank encoder adapters with quantization‑aware training.
problem_solved: Deploying large foundation segmentation models in clinical settings is limited by compute, memory, and the need to preserve structural fidelity in medical images; this work addresses parameter-efficiency and post-training quantization accuracy for CXR segmentation.
method: Two-stage fine-tuning: (1) adaptive low‑rank (LoRA) encoder adaptation that allocates rank per layer to maximize parameter efficiency, (2) full quantization‑aware training (QAT) with selective mixed‑precision (INT8) to maintain structural details.
Selective precision strategy: keep clinically sensitive components at higher precision while aggressively quantizing others to reduce model size and inference cost.
End-to-end segmentation fine-tuning on CXR data to validate that reduced-parameter, quantized models retain clinical segmentation quality.
impact: Enables practical on-device or edge deployment of high-performing medical segmentation models by cutting memory/compute requirements while preserving diagnostic-grade structure — useful for ML engineers, model deployers, and clinical-AI teams.
